stem:
An electrochemical cell is constructed using two half-cells.

- a $\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-$ half-cell
- an $\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}$ half-cell

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the material used for the electrode in each half-cell.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The cell is operated at $298\text{ K}$.

The $\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-$ half-cell has standard concentrations.

The $\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}$ half-cell has $[\text{Mn}^{3+}] = 0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ and $[\text{Mn}^{2+}] = 0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Use the Nernst equation to calculate the electrode potential, $E$, of the $\text{Mn}^{3+}/\text{Mn}^{2+}$ half-cell under these conditions.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the overall cell reaction that occurs.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An aqueous solution of copper(II) sulfate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. A current of $1.50\text{ A}$ is passed for $3.00$ hours. $5.09\text{ g}$ of copper is deposited on the cathode.

The charge on one electron is $-1.60 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$.

The relative atomic mass of copper is $63.5$.

Use these data to calculate an experimentally determined value for the Avogadro constant, $L$. Give your answer to **three** significant figures.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why magnesium metal cannot be obtained by the electrolysis of dilute aqueous magnesium sulfate. Your answer should include data from the *Data Booklet*.
